Take home the ring you created.

workshopPackages.fullDescription: Discover Sri Lanka’s beautiful gemstones, choose your favourite and create a ring around it. Our skilled jeweller will help turn your idea into something truly personal.

pricingExplanation: You’re not just buying a ring. You’re making one. Every experience includes real silver, professional tools, hands-on learning and guidance from a skilled local jeweller. Our prices reflect quality craftsmanship and fair compensation for our artisans.

workshopFaqs.question: Where can I make my own jewellery in Sri Lanka?
workshopFaqs.answer: The Ring Experience offers guided ring-making workshops at 63/1 Porutota Road in Negombo, Sri Lanka. Beginners can design a ring and join suitable making stages with an artisan. Compare workshop options and send your date and group size before visiting.

workshopFaqs.question: Where can I order custom jewellery in Sri Lanka?
workshopFaqs.answer: At The Ring Experience you can discuss a personal ring design in Negombo. Send the piece you want, a reference image, metal and stone preferences, budget range and deadline. We review custom requests and explain feasibility, price and timing before confirming; rings are our hands-on specialty and other jewellery is assessed individually.

workshopFaqs.question: What should I tell a jeweller to design a custom ring?
workshopFaqs.answer: Start with the occasion and wearer, intended finger or ring size, metal, preferred gemstone, reference images, budget range and the date you need it. If you want to work at the bench yourself, say so. You can leave choices undecided and discuss them with the artisan.

workshopFaqs.question: Can I make wedding rings or marriage bands with my partner?
workshopFaqs.answer: You can ask us to plan a guided session for two wedding bands. Send your designs, ring sizes, metal preferences and deadline before booking. We confirm which stages you can make, what the artisan completes, the total cost and when the rings will be ready.

workshopFaqs.question: Can I design an engagement ring at the workshop?
workshopFaqs.answer: Yes, start by sending your design idea, preferred metal and gemstone. Intricate settings need specialist work and may require more than one visit. An artisan reviews feasibility, availability and completion time before you commit.

workshopFaqs.question: Do you make silver and gold jewellery?
workshopFaqs.answer: Our ring-making experiences include silver crafting. Gold designs are discussed on request. Confirm the exact metal purity, included weight, additional material charges and price basis for your design before booking.

workshopFaqs.question: Can I order a 22K gold wedding or engagement ring?
workshopFaqs.answer: Tell us the purity you prefer and how you intend to wear the ring. We discuss gold designs on request; an artisan must review the design, setting, metal availability, weight and current quote before confirming whether a particular 22K piece is suitable or possible.

workshopFaqs.question: Can I buy a Ceylon sapphire or Sri Lankan gemstone through you?
workshopFaqs.answer: Tell us the stone and design you want. We can discuss sourcing a suitable gem for a ring, subject to availability and review; we do not list unverified stones as in stock. Ask for identity, treatment disclosure, origin evidence, any independent laboratory report and a written price before committing. A stone sold or cut in Sri Lanka is not automatically Sri Lankan-mined.

workshopFaqs.question: Are your gemstones natural, untreated and certified?
workshopFaqs.answer: Those are questions about an individual stone, not a blanket promise. Before agreeing to a gemstone purchase, request its identity, natural or laboratory-grown status, known treatments and the specific report, if any. An origin opinion is not the same as proof of where a stone was sold or cut.

workshopFaqs.question: What makes a sapphire suitable for an engagement ring?
workshopFaqs.answer: Discuss colour, cut, size, setting, daily wear and any treatments. Sapphire is a durable gem, but its setting and care still matter. Request information about the actual stone and an independent report when origin or treatment affects your decision.

workshopFaqs.question: Can I use my own sapphire or heirloom gold?
workshopFaqs.answer: Send photos and documents before you visit. An artisan needs to inspect the stone or metal and review the new design. Existing materials cannot always be safely reused, and testing, reworking or setting can change the price and timeline.

workshopFaqs.question: Can I order a necklace, name pendant or chain?
workshopFaqs.answer: Rings are the focus of our hands-on workshop. You can send another jewellery idea for individual review. We will tell you whether an artisan can take it on, what the process involves and whether it is a custom order rather than a workshop project.

workshopFaqs.question: How soon can a custom ring be ready for a holiday or proposal?
workshopFaqs.answer: Tell us the exact date and your design. A simple band may fit a workshop session, while sourcing a gemstone, setting, engraving or other specialist work can take longer. We confirm a realistic handover date after reviewing the materials and design; an inquiry alone is not a completion promise.

workshopFaqs.question: How much does a custom ring or gemstone cost?
workshopFaqs.answer: The total depends on workshop choice, metal purity and weight, ring design, gemstone, setting, engraving and finishing. Ask for a written breakdown of inclusions and extras. We quote gold and individual gemstone options only after reviewing the design and available materials.

workshopFaqs.question: Are gemstones, engraving and extra metal included?
workshopFaqs.answer: Essential includes 4g of sterling silver; gemstones and settings cost extra. Signature Gem Discovery includes 6g of silver, LKR 5,000 toward one gemstone and one standard setting. Ceremony includes 8g of silver, LKR 8,000 toward one gemstone, one standard setting and personalised engraving. Extra silver costs LKR 2,000 per gram in each package. You pay the difference for a gemstone above the allowance; advanced settings and gold are quoted before you agree.

workshopFaqs.question: Will I make the whole ring myself?
workshopFaqs.answer: Your involvement depends on the design, techniques and session. Tell us if doing as much as possible yourself is your priority. We can recommend a simpler project and explain which technical stages an artisan will handle for safety and accuracy.

workshopFaqs.question: Can I bring a gemstone or old ring to use in a new design?
workshopFaqs.answer: Send clear photos and any stone or metal documentation first. An artisan needs to review the condition, material and proposed design. Bringing a piece does not guarantee that it can be reused or set during your session.

workshopFaqs.question: How do I choose my ring size?
workshopFaqs.answer: The intended finger should be measured for the width and profile you want. Bring a well-fitting ring if useful, and tell us which sizing system you know. A home measurement is a starting point; confirm the fit with the artisan before making.

workshopFaqs.question: Is a ring-making workshop a good activity before a flight?
workshopFaqs.answer: Only if your itinerary allows enough time. Tell us your flight and onward travel plans before requesting a session. Allow time for the full workshop and a separate airport journey; we do not promise airport transfer times or completion before a flight without reviewing your plans.

workshopFaqs.question: Where is The Ring Experience in Negombo?
workshopFaqs.answer: Find us at 63/1 Porutota Road, Negombo 11500, Sri Lanka. Use the Google Maps link for directions and contact us before travelling to confirm your session and arrival details.

workshopFaqs.question: Does submitting a request confirm my booking?
workshopFaqs.answer: No. A form submission or WhatsApp message starts your inquiry. Your session is confirmed only when we agree the date, availability, design and booking details with you.

journalPosts.title: Make a silver ring in Negombo: what to expect at the workbench
journalPosts.description: A practical guide to a guided silver ring-making workshop in Negombo, from choosing a design to finishing your ring.
journalPosts.intro: A handmade ring can carry a memory of a place more vividly than a souvenir from a shelf. At The Ring Experience in Negombo, you choose a design and take part in making it with an artisan beside you. Here is what that actually means before you reserve a session.

sections.heading: Start with a ring you can make in the time available
paragraphs: A band, a texture, an inscription or a stone can change the work involved. Bring a photo or a sketch if you have one, but keep an open mind: an artisan can help translate the idea into a design that suits your chosen workshop, the metal available and the time you have.

Tell us if you especially want to use the tools yourself. Some stages require close guidance or an artisan to take over for accuracy and safety. The amount of hands-on work depends on the design and techniques, so it is worth discussing before you book.

sections.heading: What happens during the session?
paragraphs: You begin by talking through the size, shape and finish. At the workbench, you learn how a ring is measured, shaped and refined. Depending on the design, you may saw, form, texture or polish parts of your piece with guidance. Your artisan oversees the technical stages and finishing.

A simple band is a good first project. Stone setting and more intricate details take additional time and may change the materials and final price. Our workshop page lists the current options; we confirm the exact inclusions and any extras with you before the booking is agreed.

sections.heading: Why silver is a popular starting point
paragraphs: Sterling silver is commonly used for jewellery. It contains 92.5% silver and 7.5% other metal, usually copper, according to The Silver Institute. That alloy makes it a practical material for a wearable ring while retaining the look of silver.

Silver can develop tarnish over time. A soft polishing cloth and dry storage help keep it looking bright. If you want a different finish or a gemstone, ask what is suitable for your design and session.

sections.heading: Planning a visit in Negombo
paragraphs: Set aside the time shown for the workshop you choose, plus some flexibility if your ring has extra details. If you are flying or travelling onward the same day, tell us before reserving. Send your preferred date, the number of makers and any design ideas; we will reply with availability and a clear description of what the session includes.

journalPosts.title: Silver or gold for a handmade ring? A maker’s guide
journalPosts.description: Compare sterling silver with 14k and 18k gold for a personal ring, including purity, design choices and questions to ask before a workshop.
journalPosts.intro: Choosing the metal is part of choosing the story of your ring. Sterling silver makes a beautiful first piece; gold may suit a long-term heirloom. The right answer depends on your design, budget, colour preference and what is available for your session.

sections.heading: What does “sterling silver” mean?
paragraphs: Sterling silver contains 92.5% silver and 7.5% other metal, most commonly copper. The mix gives jewellery more practical strength than pure silver. It has a bright, cool colour and can be polished again as it wears.

Silver naturally tarnishes when exposed to the environment. That surface change is different from the metal being lost. Store your ring dry and clean it gently with a suitable jewellery cloth; ask a jeweller before using cleaners on a ring with gemstones.

sections.heading: What do 14k and 18k gold mean?
paragraphs: Gold caratage describes the proportion of gold in an alloy. Eighteen carat gold is 75% gold; 14 carat gold is about 58.5% gold. The other metals affect colour and working properties. Yellow, rose and white gold are not interchangeable labels for one identical alloy.

A higher gold content does not automatically make a design better. Think about how you want the ring to look, how it will be worn and what the finished piece will weigh. Ask for the metal purity and a written price basis before committing to a gold design.

source.label: World Gold Council: gold jewellery purity and colour

sections.heading: How does metal choice change a workshop?
paragraphs: The techniques, material cost and time can differ by design. Our published workshop options focus on a guided making experience; gold is discussed on request. We confirm the current material availability, amount of metal, additional charges and what you can do yourself before agreeing on a session.

For your first ring, start with the shape and meaning you want. A slim silver band with a personal texture can feel as significant as a more elaborate gold piece. If a gemstone matters most, mention it early so the artisan can advise on a suitable setting and timetable.

sections.heading: A simple checklist before booking
paragraphs: Ask which metal and how much of it is included, whether a gemstone or engraving costs extra, how much time your design needs, and which parts you can make yourself. Send a reference image if you have one. Clear answers make it easier to choose the workshop that fits your visit.

journalPosts.title: A Sri Lankan jewellery-making experience to take home
journalPosts.description: Explore how a guided ring-making activity in Negombo turns a Sri Lanka visit into a personal piece made with an artisan.
journalPosts.intro: When you visit Sri Lanka, the best mementos often come from the time you spent making or learning something. A ring-making workshop offers a pause from sightseeing: you sit with an artisan, work with your hands and leave with a piece connected to your own story.

sections.heading: An activity you can shape around your visit
paragraphs: The Ring Experience is a guided jewellery workshop in Negombo. Guests come alone, with friends or as a couple. You do not need prior experience. You can begin with a simple band, explore a texture or ask whether a more detailed design is possible in the time you have.

The workshop is personal because the choices are yours. Size, finish, a small symbol or a gemstone can give a ring meaning, but each addition has a different cost and time requirement. We discuss those details before confirming your booking.

sections.heading: Meet the process, not just the finished product
paragraphs: At the workbench you see how decisions about shape and material turn into a wearable piece. An artisan guides the tools and the technical steps, while you take part where your chosen design allows. If you want a particularly hands-on session, say so when you inquire so we can recommend a suitable project.
The finished ring is only one part of what you take away. You also know the decisions and work that went into it, and can remember the people and place connected to that moment.

sections.heading: Choose the right session
paragraphs: Our workshops vary in length and scope. Compare the current package descriptions, then tell us your preferred date, the number of guests and any ring ideas. We can clarify material inclusions, gemstone choices and extras before you reserve.

If you are staying in Negombo briefly or have onward travel, leave enough time for the full session. A booking request starts a conversation; it becomes a confirmed visit when we agree on availability and the details together.

sections.heading: Make it part of your Sri Lanka story
paragraphs: A personal ring is useful long after a trip ends. It can mark a first solo journey, a shared holiday, an anniversary or simply an afternoon spent learning a craft. Browse our guest gallery for ideas, then bring your own. We will help you find a design that suits the workshop.

journalPosts.title: Make your own wedding rings in Sri Lanka: a couple’s guide
journalPosts.description: Questions to ask before making wedding bands together in Negombo: design, sizing, metal, workshop time, engraving and finishing.
journalPosts.intro: Making wedding bands together can turn a practical decision into a shared memory. A guided ring-making session in Negombo lets you shape a design with an artisan. Plan the details before a wedding date so the finished rings feel right and there is enough time for the work.

sections.heading: Can we make two wedding rings in one session?
paragraphs: Tell us that you want two bands when you inquire. The design of each ring, material, sizes and finishing work determine how long the session needs. A simple pair may be more realistic for a first workshop than two intricate designs. We will confirm whether your preferred session accommodates both rings and what is included before you book.

You can choose matching profiles or two different rings with a shared detail, such as a texture. Bring reference images and mention any date by which the rings must be ready. We cannot promise a particular design or same-day completion until an artisan has reviewed it.

sections.heading: Which metal should we choose for wedding bands?
paragraphs: Consider the look you love, how often you will wear the rings and your budget. Sterling silver is 92.5% silver and can be polished as it ages. Gold is usually alloyed for jewellery; 18 carat is 75% gold and 14 carat is about 58.5% gold. Gold material and workshop availability need to be confirmed for your particular design.

Ask for the metal purity, amount of metal, any extra charge and the final price basis in writing. Our metal comparison guide explains the practical differences without treating one metal as the only correct choice.

source.label: World Gold Council: about gold jewellery

sections.heading: How do we get the sizes right?
paragraphs: Have each finger measured for the intended band width. A wide band can feel different from a narrow one, and hands can change size through the day. If a ring is a surprise, ask an artisan what measurements or an existing ring would be useful rather than relying on a guess.
Discuss resizing and finishing before work begins, especially if a stone, pattern or inscription runs around the band. Not every design can be adjusted in the same way.

sections.heading: Can we add an engraving or gemstone?
paragraphs: Possibly, depending on the design and workshop. Engraving, stone selection and setting can add time and cost. Send the inscription and gemstone idea in advance; we will tell you what can be done in your session and what an artisan would complete for you.
Before confirming, ask which steps you will personally do, what the artisan will do, the total cost for two rings, and when the rings will be ready. That makes the day itself more relaxed.

journalPosts.title: Designing an engagement ring in Sri Lanka: questions to ask first
journalPosts.description: A practical guide to engagement ring design, gemstones, settings, metal, sizing and what a hands-on workshop can involve.
journalPosts.intro: An engagement ring can begin with a shared design conversation, even if the proposal is a surprise. A workshop is an opportunity to explore the shape, material and meaning of a ring with an artisan. More complex stone-set designs need an early discussion about the work, cost and timing.

sections.heading: Can I make an engagement ring myself?
paragraphs: You can take part in a guided ring-making experience as a beginner. The exact hands-on stages depend on the design. A plain or textured band is different from a ring with a delicate stone setting: an artisan may need to handle specialist work for safety and accuracy.

Send a reference image, desired metal, preferred stone and travel dates before booking. We will explain what you can do at the bench, what requires an artisan and whether the design fits an available workshop. Do not assume every engagement-ring design can be finished during one visit.

sections.heading: Diamond, sapphire or another gemstone?
paragraphs: Start with the wearer’s preferences and everyday activities. If you are considering a diamond, the GIA 4Cs—cut, colour, clarity and carat weight—help describe its quality. Ask for reliable documentation and disclosure of any treatment or whether a stone is natural or laboratory-grown.

Coloured gemstones deserve a conversation about durability, setting and care. Sapphire and ruby are often considered for rings, but hardness is only one aspect of durability. Ask about the exact stone, any treatments and the setting that will protect it. We confirm stone availability rather than promising a particular gem on the website.

sections.heading: What setting and metal suit the design?
paragraphs: A low profile may be comfortable for everyday wear; a raised setting changes the look and may catch more easily on clothing. Discuss the shape and size of the stone with an artisan before settling on a sketch. The setting, band width and metal all affect the technical work and price.

Sterling silver has a bright cool tone. Gold can be yellow, rose or white depending on its alloy. Ask for the precise purity and a full price breakdown, including the stone and setting. Gold options are discussed on request and are subject to availability.

sections.heading: What if the proposal is a surprise?
paragraphs: An existing ring worn on the correct finger can help with sizing, but do not assume it will fit an engagement ring with a different band width. You can also plan a shared design conversation after the proposal. Tell us your deadline, budget range and whether you need the final ring on a specific date.

A clear inquiry should ask about metal and stone availability, sizing, the part you will make, artisan finishing, total price and completion timing. We can recommend a suitable next step after reviewing those details.

journalPosts.title: Sri Lankan gemstones for a personal ring: sapphire and beyond
journalPosts.description: How to choose a coloured gemstone for a handmade ring in Sri Lanka, including sapphire durability, treatments, setting and care questions.
journalPosts.intro: Sri Lanka is closely associated with coloured gemstones. If you would like a gem in the ring you make in Negombo, start with the colour and story you want, then ask about the actual stone and the work required to set it securely.

sections.heading: Is a sapphire a good choice for a ring?
paragraphs: Sapphire is corundum and ranks 9 on the Mohs hardness scale, according to GIA. That helps it resist scratches, although hardness alone does not mean a gem cannot chip or need careful cleaning. The way a ring is worn, the stone shape and the setting matter too.

Sapphires come in more than one colour. If you have a specific shade or shape in mind, ask what is actually available for your date and budget. A website photograph is an idea, not a promise that an identical stone is in stock.

sections.heading: What should I ask about a coloured gem?
paragraphs: Ask the name of the stone, whether it is natural or laboratory-grown, whether it has been treated, and whether any report or documentation is included. Gemstone descriptions and treatments affect what you are buying and how you should care for it.
A coloured gemstone engagement ring also needs a setting suited to the gem and the wearer’s routine. Discuss the design with an artisan before choosing a stone based only on its colour or a photo.

sections.heading: Can I set the stone in my workshop?
paragraphs: That depends on the stone, design, available tools and session length. Gemstone setting is technical and an artisan may need to do that step. Tell us in advance if setting a stone yourself is important to you, and we will be clear about the stages you can join.

Ask whether the stone and setting are included in the workshop price, what additional work is needed and when the ring can be collected. A simple textured band without a gem may be the better choice if your time is short.

sections.heading: How do I care for a gemstone ring?
paragraphs: Care varies with the specific gem, treatments and setting. Take a ring off for activities that could knock it against a hard surface. Ask the artisan for care instructions for your exact ring rather than assuming one cleaning method suits all gems.
If you already own a gemstone you hope to use, ask us to review it before booking. We cannot promise that every existing stone can be safely set in a workshop design.

journalPosts.title: How to care for silver, gold and gemstone rings after your workshop
journalPosts.description: Simple care for your handmade ring: silver tarnish, gentle cleaning, safe storage and why gemstone treatments matter.
journalPosts.intro: Your ring leaves the bench with a finish you helped choose. Keeping it looking good starts with knowing its metal, stone and setting. Ask for care instructions for your exact piece before leaving the studio.

sections.heading: What does 925 mean on a silver ring?
paragraphs: Sterling silver is 92.5% silver, usually alloyed with copper for jewellery. The number 925 describes that fineness. Silver can tarnish as it reacts with its surroundings; a surface colour change does not by itself mean the ring is fake.

For a plain silver band, use a suitable soft jewellery polishing cloth with a light touch. Keep pieces dry and separate during storage. Tell your jeweller if you want to preserve a deliberately darkened texture: polishing can change that finish.

sections.heading: Does gold need different care?
paragraphs: Gold jewellery is an alloy, and its colour and properties depend on the metals mixed with gold. Eighteen carat is 75% gold; 14 carat is about 58.5%. Higher purity does not make a finished ring immune to scratching or wear.

Keep your ring away from activities that knock or distort it. Before using a chemical cleaner, check that it suits the whole piece, including solder joints, plating, stones and any special finish. Ask an artisan to inspect a loose stone or damaged setting rather than continuing to wear it.

source.label: World Gold Council: gold purity and colour

sections.heading: Can I clean every gemstone ring the same way?
paragraphs: No. The gem and any treatments matter. GIA recommends warm soapy water for moonstone and advises against ultrasonic or steam cleaning. Moonstone also needs protection from hard knocks and sudden temperature changes.

Sapphire is harder, but filled or dyed stones need different care from untreated material. Ask which treatments are known for your stone before choosing a cleaner. When that information is missing, ask the maker for advice before trying a home cleaning method.

sections.heading: What should I ask before taking my ring home?
paragraphs: Confirm the metal purity, stone identity, known treatments, care method and whether the finish needs special handling. Ask how to arrange a fit or setting inspection if something changes. Keep your receipt and any gemstone documentation together.
If you want a ring for everyday wear, tell us during the design conversation. We can discuss its width, finish, stone choice and setting before you choose the details.

journalPosts.title: Ring size and fit: what to check before making your own ring
journalPosts.description: A practical sizing checklist for custom rings, wedding bands and surprise gifts, including band width, existing rings and resizing questions.
journalPosts.intro: A personal ring should feel right as well as look right. A number from an online chart can start the conversation, but the final fit belongs to the actual finger, band width and shape you choose.

sections.heading: Bring the sizing system, not just a number
paragraphs: Ring sizes are labelled differently across countries. Tell the artisan whether your measurement uses UK letters, US numbers or an inside diameter in millimetres. Do not send a bare number without the system.

An existing ring can be useful if it fits the intended finger. Tell us which hand and finger it is worn on. For a surprise gift, send the information you have and ask what can be measured reliably before choosing a design.

sections.heading: Why does band width matter?
paragraphs: A broad band can feel different from a narrow ring in the same nominal size. The inner profile also affects comfort. Try a sample close to your intended design and confirm the fit with the artisan before work begins.

Your hands can change through the day and with temperature. Avoid deciding solely from a tight strip of paper or a measurement taken when your hands feel unusually swollen. A home measurement is a guide, not a guaranteed final fit.

sections.heading: Can a finished ring be resized?
paragraphs: Ask before making it. The answer depends on its metal, construction, pattern and stone setting. A plain band and a design with stones or engraving all the way around it present different challenges.

If you are ordering wedding bands, allow time to check both finished rings before the ceremony. Mention your deadline early and ask what adjustments could involve; do not assume every ring can be resized immediately or without changing its appearance.

sections.heading: Send a useful custom-ring inquiry
paragraphs: Include the occasion, intended finger, sizing system, preferred band width, metal, finish and any stone or engraving ideas. Add a reference photograph if it helps explain the style.
Our ring planner lets you record those choices before contacting the Negombo workshop. Leave a field undecided if you are unsure, then confirm the fit and design with the artisan.

journalPosts.title: A creative thing to do in Negombo: make a ring at the workbench
journalPosts.description: Planning activities in Negombo, Sri Lanka? See how a private jewellery workshop fits a solo visit, couples trip or short stay.
journalPosts.intro: If you want an activity in Negombo that leaves you with something personal, spend part of your visit making a ring. The Ring Experience offers guided sessions with an artisan, so you can explore a craft without arriving with jewellery-making skills.

sections.heading: What makes it different from buying a souvenir?
paragraphs: You choose details and join the making process. A shape, a hammered texture or an inscription can connect the piece to your trip. Your artisan explains which stages you can take part in and which technical work they need to complete.

Come with an idea or begin with a simple band. The design, materials and amount of hands-on work are agreed before your session. A workshop is a shared making experience, and the finished piece reflects the decisions you bring to it.

sections.heading: Is it an activity for couples or solo travellers?
paragraphs: Both can inquire. Couples may want to make two rings side by side; a solo traveller may want a personal memento. Friends can also ask about joining together. Confirm the number of makers and the total cost when choosing a session.
For wedding bands, an engagement design or a milestone gift, send your ideas in advance. A detailed stone-set ring may need more time and artisan finishing than a straightforward first project.

sections.heading: Can I fit it into a short Negombo stay?
paragraphs: Compare the current session lengths on our workshop page and leave some flexibility around your chosen time. Tell us if you are planning an arrival-day activity or have a flight afterward. Travel time, traffic and your airport requirements need their own allowance.
Do not reserve a complex ring on the assumption that it will be ready before a flight. We review your design and timing, then confirm whether a suitable session is available.

sections.heading: Where do I go, and how do I book?
paragraphs: The Ring Experience is at 63/1 Porutota Road, Negombo 11500, Sri Lanka. Use our Google Maps profile for directions and guest reviews. Contact us before setting out so we can confirm your appointment and arrival details.

Send your preferred date, number of makers and any design references. We reply with availability, materials, costs and timing. An inquiry becomes a booking only when we have agreed the details with you.

journalPosts.title: Creative things to do in Sri Lanka: make something to take home
journalPosts.description: Looking for hands-on activities in Sri Lanka? Explore batik, handloom, pottery and a guided jewellery-making workshop in Negombo.
journalPosts.intro: Beaches, wildlife and historic places are only part of a Sri Lanka trip. If you enjoy meeting makers and learning with your hands, leave room for a craft experience too. A piece you help make carries the memory of the place in a different way from one you buy.

sections.heading: Look for living crafts, not just souvenirs
paragraphs: Batik, handloom weaving and pottery are among the crafts highlighted by Sri Lanka Tourism. Workshops and demonstrations vary by place and maker, so check directly with a host before travelling. Ask whether you will observe, take part in a short lesson or make a finished item.

A good craft stop has enough time to learn a little about the tools, materials and people involved. If you visit a working studio, follow the maker’s safety guidance and ask before taking photographs.

sections.heading: Make a ring in Negombo
paragraphs: At The Ring Experience, a local artisan guides you through choices for a personal ring and helps you take part in its making. It works as a creative stop for solo travellers, couples and friends, including beginners. The amount of tool work you can do depends on the ring design and the workshop you choose.

Silver is a common starting point. If you are considering gold, a gemstone or engraving, share the idea in advance so the artisan can explain suitable materials, time and any additional cost. Compare the current workshop options and agree the details before treating an inquiry as a confirmed appointment.

sections.heading: Fit a creative stop into a real travel day
paragraphs: If Negombo is your first or last stop in Sri Lanka, combine a prearranged workshop with time to see the fishing town, canal, lagoon or beach. Our Negombo activity guide gives a loose morning-to-evening plan. Leave enough room for travel and any onward flight rather than scheduling a detailed ring just before departure.

Elsewhere on the island, look for craft hosts whose activity fits the place you are already visiting. Availability, opening hours and whether you can take a finished piece with you should be confirmed with each host.

sections.heading: Questions to ask before choosing a craft activity
paragraphs: What will I actually do with my hands? How long does it take? What materials are included? Does a professional finish any technical stages? Can I bring the item home on the day? These questions help you choose a workshop that matches your expectations.

For our ring-making sessions, send your date, group size and any ring ideas through the booking page. We will reply with availability and the scope of the session. If you are still exploring, start with the visitor guide to see how ring making works.

journalPosts.title: Buying a Ceylon sapphire in Sri Lanka: questions worth asking
journalPosts.description: Before choosing a Sri Lankan sapphire for a custom ring, ask about origin, natural or lab-grown status, treatments, reports, setting and the actual stone.
journalPosts.intro: A blue sapphire can be the centre of an engagement ring or a personal piece. “Ceylon sapphire” is an origin description, not a substitute for checking the specific gem. Here is how to have a clear conversation before buying or setting one in Sri Lanka.

sections.heading: Does buying a sapphire in Sri Lanka prove it was mined here?
paragraphs: No. Sri Lanka is both a source of gemstones and a cutting, treatment and trading centre for material from elsewhere. A seller’s location, a workshop visit or a photograph cannot establish where a particular stone formed.

If origin affects your decision or the price, ask for an independent laboratory report on the exact stone that includes an origin opinion when possible. Even specialist origin determination can be uncertain, particularly after treatment. Read the report’s wording rather than assuming every certificate proves “Ceylon” origin.

source.label: GIA: Sri Lanka, an island of jewels

sections.heading: Which facts belong on the invoice or report?
paragraphs: Ask for the gem’s identity, measurements, weight, colour and whether it is natural or laboratory-grown. Request disclosure of known treatments such as heat or diffusion, the report issuer and number if a report is included, and a price for that specific stone. Confirm what the seller will provide in writing before paying.

A gemstone report describes the stone examined; it is not a promise about how a finished ring will wear. Check that the report details match the gem you receive. If a report is important to you, agree on that requirement before an artisan begins the setting.

sections.heading: Can a sapphire be worn every day?
paragraphs: Sapphire is corundum, a relatively durable material often selected for rings. But an exposed setting can still be knocked, and treatments can affect care. A stone’s shape, depth and size influence which setting will protect it and how the ring feels to wear.
Ask an artisan to review both the stone and the design. Avoid choosing an engagement-ring setting solely from a photograph; the actual gem and the wearer’s routine matter.

sections.heading: What can The Ring Experience arrange?
paragraphs: Our Negombo studio can discuss a gemstone idea for a custom ring and review whether a suitable stone can be sourced for the design. We do not represent a specific sapphire or a certificate as available until it has been individually confirmed. Tell us your preferred colour, shape, budget range and date.

We will explain the workshop choice, what making stages you can join, which work an artisan must complete, and any stone, setting or material charges before you commit. For a proposal or flight deadline, ask for a realistic handover date rather than assuming same-day completion.

journalPosts.title: How to commission custom jewellery during a Sri Lanka trip
journalPosts.description: A practical inquiry checklist for custom rings, wedding bands and engagement designs: metal, gemstone, budget, making involvement and travel deadline.
journalPosts.intro: You may want a ring you helped make, or a design that needs more of an artisan’s specialist work. Either way, a good first message lets a workshop tell you what is realistic before your holiday schedule or proposal date is fixed.

sections.heading: What should I put in my first message?
paragraphs: Tell us what piece you want and for whom: a personal ring, two wedding bands, an engagement design or a gift. Include a sketch or reference photo, the metal and stone you prefer, your approximate budget, the number of makers and the date you need the finished piece.

If you want to do as much as possible yourself, say that at the start. A simple band offers different hands-on possibilities from a delicate stone-set design. We can then explain which stages you can join and which an artisan would do.

sections.heading: What if I want gold or a Sri Lankan gemstone?
paragraphs: Gold is discussed on request. Ask about purity, estimated metal weight, how the metal price is calculated and how a design change affects cost. For a gemstone, ask about the exact stone, identity, known treatments, any independent report and evidence for an origin claim. A “Ceylon” label alone is not enough to establish origin.
Choosing a stone may involve sourcing and specialist setting work. We confirm availability and a quote for the proposed materials before treating an inquiry as an order.

sections.heading: Make at the bench or commission a finished piece?
paragraphs: The Ring Experience specialises in guided ring-making sessions in Negombo. You choose the design and work with an artisan where the techniques allow. Complex rings can need additional artisan finishing. Other jewellery ideas can be sent for individual review; do not assume that a chain or pendant is a standard workshop item.

Ask for a written explanation of inclusions, extra metal, stone and setting charges, likely handover and any later work. That helps you decide whether the experience, the commissioned piece or a simpler design best fits your trip.

sections.heading: Can I have it ready before I fly home?
paragraphs: Share the flight date and allow time for the workshop and travel separately. A design with a sourced stone, engraving or specialised setting may need longer. The artisan reviews feasibility and confirms a realistic timeline before you rely on a collection date.
The first message begins the conversation; it does not reserve a session or guarantee completion. Use the design planner for your notes, then send an inquiry with your preferred dates.
